subject: LLM data stewardship & subprocessor snapshot — prompt/response entitlements
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@clinicahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben McDowell <ben.mcdowell@clinicahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LLM data use commitments / subprocessor snapshot request

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking time with our security & legal team last week. To move our pilot forward, Legal needs a few clarifications and artifacts before we can sign the DPA addendum:

1) Training/Model Improvement: we need a clear, contractual statement of whether Redwood will use Clinica customer interactions to improve any models (including internal fine-tuning or re-training) or derivatives of them. If you cannot provide a blanket prohibition, please describe exact use cases and opt-out controls.

2) Prompt/Response Ownership: our product team wants to confirm that prompts we send and the responses returned are not claimed by Redwood as customer-facing IP unless explicitly licensed. We need a short clause that guarantees our rights to outputs and any generated artifacts.

3) Subprocessor inventory & residency: please provide a current snapshot of subprocessors involved in processing (storage, inference, telemetry) and indicate which ones may cross borders. For anything that routes through non-US locations, we need the option to restrict routing for our data.

4) Evidence pack: sample logs/audit artifacts showing how you isolate a tenant's KV cache and how prefix caching would be scoped for our account. Not a full export, but a demo dataset and manifest showing what we can expect operationally.

We can accept these as attachments or a link to a secure folder. Ben and I would ideally review a DPA redline by next Tuesday to stay on schedule (pilot start targeted 9/27).

Thanks,
Anna Liu
Head of Legal, Clinica Health
anna.liu@clinicahealth.com

(Attachments: none)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@clinicahealth.com>
Cc: Ben McDowell <ben.mcdowell@clinicahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM data use commitments / subprocessor snapshot request

Anna — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on making this as transparent as possible. Quick plan and ownership on our side:

- David will pull the subprocessor inventory snapshot and the short manifest for the evidence artifacts you requested. Expect a CSV + small manifest by EOD Friday (9/11).
- Marissa (CS & sales) will coordinate a short ops demo to show KV/prefix isolation and how routing controls are applied for an account. We can record that and provide sample logs.
- I'll get Legal to prepare a DPA redline focused on two discrete items you call out: (1) a model-improvement / training commitment and (2) an explicit output/custody statement.

A few clarifying Qs so we produce what you need:
1) By "prompts and responses are not claimed by Redwood," do you want an exclusive assignment of output IP to Clinica, or a guarantee that we will not assert any rights over generated outputs unless separately negotiated?
2) For residency restrictions, are you targeting strict geofencing for all inference traffic or only for stored artifacts/exports?

I'll reconvene with David & Marissa and circle back. Proposed slack call: Thu 9/10 10:00am PT to review the evidence scope. Does that work for Ben/Anna?

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft language options for Clinica DPA redline + artifacts list

Folks — putting together the artifacts Mark asked for and preliminary language options for Legal. Summary below; attachments referenced are in our secure drive and I'll export a CSV snapshot of current subprocessors (will be shared with Clinica).

Operational artifacts we will share:
- subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20260912.csv (service, vendor, role, location, contract status)
- evidence_pack_manifest.txt (what logs, ttl, and sample redacted records will look like)
- short demo recording (KV isolation + routing control walk-through)

Legal language options (two paths):

Option A — Non-adaptive training prohibition (stricter, easier for sales):
"Redwood agrees not to use Customer Data (including prompts and generated responses) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models, whether internal or external, except with Customer's prior written consent. Operational telemetry for platform stability and availability (non-LLM parameter telemetry) is excluded and anonymized as described in Appendix A."

Implication: clear for customer, but limits some platform research. Requires ops and billing to ensure flagged traffic is excluded from adaptive pipelines.

Option B — Controlled improvement with opt-out (more flexible):
"Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated signals derived from Customer Data to improve model performance, provided Customer Data used for model improvement has been expressly de-identified and only after Customer has been given the opportunity to opt out via the Customer Console or contract. Customer retains exclusive rights to outputs and generated artifacts; Redwood will not assert ownership of prompts or responses except as necessary for debugging and to comply with law."

Specifics re: Outputs/Ownership (common clause we should include):
"Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data, including prompts and any outputs generated by the Service. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide license to any service-generated artifacts necessary to exercise their rights under this agreement. Redwood will not claim derivative ownership absent a separate agreement."

Operational asks for engineering before we share artifacts:
- Confirm which telemetry buckets are considered "LLM model training pipelines" vs platform telemetry. We need clear labels so we can produce a sanitized sample.
- Produce sample audit logs that show tenant_id scoping for prefix/KV caches (redacted ids).

I'll draft the DPA redline using Option A as the safe default and note Option B as negotiable. Markus — do you want us to surface both options in the redline or present the stricter commit first?

Thanks,
David
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20260912.csv; evidence_pack_manifest.txt)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@clinicahealth.com>, Ben McDowell <ben.mcdowell@clinicahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM data use commitments / subprocessor snapshot request

Anna, Ben — thanks for your patience. Please find the deliverables attached to this thread:

- Clinica_DPA_redline_20260914.pdf (David drafted a redline; Option A is marked as the default with commentary on Option B if you prefer an opt-out approach)
- subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20260912.csv (current vendor roles and locations; columns: vendor, role, primary_region, has_access_to_plaintext)
- evidence_pack_manifest.txt (short manifest describing log samples, anonymization steps, and the recorded KV isolation demo)

Short answers to your original list:
1) Training/Model Improvement: We can commit contractually to "no use for model improvement" by default (Option A). If you need a pathway to allow aggregated, de-identified signals to inform generic model improvements, we can document Option B and expose an explicit opt-out toggle in the Console — but that will be a separate negotiated term.

2) Prompt/Response Ownership: Redwood will not claim ownership of prompts or generated outputs. The redline includes the clause that "Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data, prompts, and outputs; Redwood will not assert derivative ownership absent a separate written agreement."

3) Subprocessors & Residency: the CSV shows which subprocessors may process data outside the US. For any route that would move Clinica data outside the US we will apply geofencing controls at the account level; we can enumerate which vendors will be excluded if you choose strict geofencing.

4) Evidence pack: attached manifest describes what you'll receive in the secure folder. The demo recording will be uploaded and shared as a private link after you sign a standard NDA for operational artifacts.

Next steps:
- If this looks good we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to go through the redline on Thu 9/17 10:00am PT. I'll also send the DocuSign link for the DPA once we close language on the training commitment.

Please confirm which option you prefer for training controls (Option A — strict ban; Option B — opt-out/anon signals). If you want the strict ban, we will mark Option A in the DPA and proceed to signature.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
(Attachments: Clinica_DPA_redline_20260914.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20260912.csv; evidence_pack_manifest.txt)
